title: Free-body diagrams
target: Draw only the external forces on one chosen object.
criteria: Choose one object and list its external interactions.
Draw force arrows in physically correct directions.
Remove velocity and net force as extra interaction arrows.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: For the free-body diagram of a crate, which list is appropriate on a rough level floor while a rope pulls it?
options: Velocity, acceleration, and momentum as three extra forces.
Earth on crate, floor normal on crate, floor friction on crate, rope on crate.
Crate on Earth, crate on floor, crate on rope only.
Only the largest force.
cpa.guide: List external interactions acting on the chosen crate.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: When drawing forces on a bicycle rider, which proposed arrow belongs to a different object?
options: Air’s force on the rider.
Earth’s force on the rider.
The rider’s force on the seat.
The seat’s force on the rider.
cpa.guide: The rider-on-seat force acts on the seat, not the rider.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A sled slides left on a rough horizontal surface after a push ends. Which direction is kinetic friction on the sled?
options: Right.
Up.
Down.
Left.
cpa.guide: Friction opposes relative sliding at the contact.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A ball is descending after release with air resistance neglected. Which forces act on it?
options: No forces because the hand released it.
Gravity down and a downward motion force.
Gravity down and an upward launch force still attached.
Gravity downward only.
cpa.guide: After release, no hand force remains; in this model only gravity acts.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A diagram already shows every individual interaction force. Should net force be added as another interaction arrow?
options: Only if velocity is positive.
No; net force is the sum of those forces, not an additional interaction.
Yes; adding it doubles the physical force correctly.
Yes; it replaces mass.
cpa.guide: A separate resultant can be labeled as a sum, but must not be counted again.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A moving cart’s force diagram includes a rightward arrow labeled velocity among the forces. What repair is appropriate?
options: Show velocity separately as motion information and omit it from the force sum.
Count velocity as an extra force in newtons.
Replace gravity with velocity.
Keep it only if the cart moves right.
cpa.guide: Velocity is measured in m/s and is not an interaction force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
